svg.text: Three channels fit side by side at 2.4 GHz. At 5 GHz, twenty-five do.
Channel 1 is 2412 MHz and every step of one adds 5 MHz, so channel 6 is 2437 MHz. Each channel is 22 MHz wide, so neighbours overlap.
Only 1, 6 and 11 sit far enough apart to stay clear
Same 5 MHz step, different base: channel 36 is 5180 MHz and channel 40 is 5200 MHz. A 20 MHz channel takes every fourth number within a band.
The break at 5350 to 5470 MHz is kept for radar and satellite, and 144 steps to 149 rather than 148 because 149 opens a new band at 5745 MHz
The rows share a width to compare how many channels fit, not bandwidth
2.4 GHz travels further and through more walls, which is exactly why it stays crowded.
Scan only 2.4 GHz and every 5 GHz network stays invisible.
